findings: G4 — create-business-process accepts a decision expressed as two plain outgoing flows off an ordinary step; modify-business-process refuses the same end state via WouldDropTheLastBranch, with a message naming the consequence. Runtime measured: both branches execute in a single instance (SysProcessElementLog, instance b54d0abf). Graded by merge base 5781c6aa5: the ACCEPTANCE is pre-existing (no such guard existed), the REFUSAL is new in this PR (FlowKindRules.cs absent at base) — so this change introduced the disagreement by guarding one door only.

The review session's pre-registered prediction that the two doors would AGREE is refuted: EnsureADefaultHasSomethingToFallBackFrom fires only on kind == Default, so a withdrawal expressed as [plain, plain] never reaches the build-side guard.

Gateway remark confirmed as predicted: on a drawn gateway element the same withdrawal is refused by the 'already has its default branch' objection (FlowKindRules.cs:302), which is why the case had to move to an ordinary step.
